correctness.rationale: Antipodal invariance gives a fair direction sign conditional on the entire unoriented vector (line and radius); independence makes the conditional joint sign law a product, including after the almost surely strict projective sort. In a generic half-turn sweep, each point changes membership once, giving counts C_j=(n+s)/2-S_j, with the other half-turn giving n-C_j. A boundary with one point places each of the open/closed counts among the two adjacent generic counts, and cannot lower the minimum below the generic one. Thus the event at threshold r is exactly |s-2S_j|≤n-2r for all j. For |s|≤n-2r of the correct parity, the confinement becomes a killed walk on sites 1,…,h-1 with endpoints a=(h-s)/2, b=(h+s)/2 and h=n-2r+2. Odd image extension at 0 and h satisfies the walk recurrence with zero boundary and the correct initial delta, so the images b+2kh and -b+2kh give binomial indices (n+s)/2+kh and r-1+kh (up to reindexing). The allowed endpoints' first indices span all but the r-1 residue class, while each of the h-1 second image sums subtracts that same class. Dividing the resulting 2^n minus h times the residue sum by 2^n proves the claim. Generic antipodal counts sum to n, giving zero past floor(n/2); r≤0 is certain. At r=1 the remaining binomials are the two extremes, and at r=2, n≥5, they have indices 1 and n-1. No assumption of identical or uniform underlying laws, or of independent order statistics, is used. For planar rows in general position, any two active rows span, so testing the generic active sets suffices for the stated zero-bias application.
